title: Validation & Early Stopping 🛑
description: Monitor validation performance and stop training at the right time.

slides.title: Validate After Every Epoch ✅
slides.content:
# Validation Loop

After each training epoch, evaluate on the validation set (no gradients).

```python
model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    for x_batch, y_batch in val_loader:
        pred = model(x_batch)
        loss = criterion(pred, y_batch)
        # accumulate
```
This gives a clean signal of generalization.

slides.title: Validation Loop Snippet
slides.codeSnippet:
model.eval()
total_val_loss = 0.0
with torch.no_grad():
    for x_batch, y_batch in val_loader:
        pred = model(x_batch)
        loss = criterion(pred, y_batch)
        total_val_loss += loss.item() * x_batch.size(0)
avg_val_loss = total_val_loss / len(val_dataset)
print(avg_val_loss)

quizData.question: Why do we use `torch.no_grad()` during validation?

options.text: To speed up and reduce memory by not tracking gradients

quizData.explanation: Gradients are not needed during evaluation; disabling them saves resources.

slides.title: Early Stopping Strategy 🛑⏰
slides.content:
## Stop Before Overfitting

Monitor validation loss. If it doesn't improve for **patience** epochs, stop training and restore the best model.

Algorithm:
1. Track best val loss and best model state.
2. If val loss improves, save state.
3. Else increment counter. If counter > patience, break.

slides.title: Early Stopping Implementation
slides.codeSnippet:
best_val_loss = float('inf')
patience = 5
counter = 0

for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    train(...)
    val_loss = validate(...)
    if val_loss < best_val_loss:
        best_val_loss = val_loss
        torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'best_model.pt')
        counter = 0
    else:
        counter += 1
        if counter >= patience:
            print("Early stopping!")
            break

quizData.question: If patience = 3 and validation loss does not improve for 3 consecutive epochs, what happens?

options.text: Training stops and best model is restored

quizData.explanation: Early stopping halts training when no improvement is seen, and we reload the best checkpoint.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Save Checkpoints Regularly

Use `torch.save({'epoch': epoch, 'model_state_dict': model.state_dict(), 'optimizer_state_dict': optimizer.state_dict(), 'loss': loss}, 'checkpoint.pt')` to resume training later.
